title: I love dental nursing – but the right workplace matters
html:
For Dental Nurse Day, Harriet Gill reflects on finding a career she loves, the demands dental nurses face and why the right working environment can make all the difference.

Dental nursing is a highly rewarding career, it can open up pathways and opportunities allowing us to build on our scope of practice and knowledge within the dental industry.

However, it is important to not underestimate the dedication, commitment and perseverance required to reach those goals.

There is certainly a lot expected of us as dental professionals. There is so much that we have to learn, retain and continue to build on throughout our career in order to perform our daily roles to the best of our abilities with optimum understanding and professionalism.

I personally absolutely adore working as a dental nurse and have truly found myself, what I enjoy most about the profession and what I’m striving towards over the past five years working in dentistry.

It is acceptable to find dental nursing difficult

I truly believe that although I will always talk about dental nursing in such a positive light along with the fact that I personally love the career, it doesn’t take away the fact that the reality of dental nursing is something which needs to be spoken about.

Alongside being extremely rewarding it can be very difficult. It is mentally and physically draining at times (which of course you can expect from any profession) but gaining an understanding on whether it is suited to you as an individual is very important.

I feel extremely grateful to work in a practice where I feel constantly supported and encouraged to be the best version of my professional self. The opportunities since gaining my qualification and General Dental Council number have been fulfilling, building on my own scope of practice is something I feel extremely lucky I continue to have the opportunity to do.

Working alongside clinicians as a team and supporting each other on a daily basis is essential. I encourage any dental nurse who is criticising themselves for not enjoying the job role to absolutely not be so hard on themselves, it is more than ok if it is not suited to you!

Finding the right place for you

But also consider your working environment, do you feel you are in the right place for you? Nobody is at fault here, it may be the fact you enjoy a certain area within dental nursing which you want to focus in on more or your learning requirements or personal circumstances have changed and a different practice or setting may be better suited to you. Please always remember that is more than acceptable.

It can become very easy to not prioritise yourself but I do believe that positivity, enjoyment and a strong support system with effective communication in the workplace allows you to perform well and strive to be the very best version of yourself as a dental nurse and dental care professional.

Always remember to believe in yourself, listen to yourself and communicate with those around you.

Happy Dental Nurse Day!
